title: AQ Podcast | What a Democratic U.S. Congress Means for the Donroe Doctrine
author: NOVEMBER 19, 2026
text:
FacebookXLinkedInThreadsEmailShare

Reading Time: < 1 minute

The blue wave in the U.S. midterms marked a before and after for the Trump administration, but what it will mean for Latin America is an open question. This is the White House most focused on the region in at least 40 years, and from Venezuela to Mexico to Cuba and Argentina, virtually every country has seen its destiny altered by Washington. A Democratic Congress could use its powers of investigation, subpoena and budget to rein in the boat strikes in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, bring scrutiny to tariffs, or investigate the deals struck to extract Venezuelan oil. Yet presidents often turn to foreign policy in their final years in office, and Trump still has 26 months left in his term. Will a divided Washington constrain him, or make him even more interventionist? Our guests are Emily Mendrala, a geopolitical strategy consultant, and Eric Jacobstein, Founder and Principal at Puentes Global Advisory.

Guests:

Emily Mendrala is a geopolitical strategy consultant. She was previously Coordinator for the Southwest Border at the White House from 2023 to 2024 and covered Cuba, Central America and regional migration as Deputy Assistant Secretary of State.

Eric Jacobstein is Founder and Principal at Puentes Global Advisory. He previously served at the White House as Special Adviser to the Vice President for the Western Hemisphere and as National Security Council Director for Central America and Cuba.

Host:

Brian Winter is editor in chief of Americas Quarterly
